source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Uncomplicated resolution of pancreatitis, because a new palpable abdominal mass is expected during recovery.","B":"Renal colic, because a pancreatic complication would not persist for several weeks after acute pancreatitis.","C":"Acute appendicitis, because post-pancreatitis fluid collections do not cause persistent upper-abdominal pain.","D":"A pancreatic pseudocyst or other post-pancreatitis pancreatic fluid collection requiring further evaluation."}}
source_row.rationale: Pancreatic fluid collections, including pseudocysts, are recognized complications of pancreatitis. Persistent pain and a new abdominal mass after pancreatitis warrant further clinical evaluation rather than being assumed to represent routine recovery.
source_row.source_detail: Clinical presentation and evaluation of pancreatic pseudocyst after pancreatitis, including persistent abdominal symptoms and mass effect. source_row.stem: Several weeks after acute pancreatitis, a client has persistent upper-abdominal pain and a newly palpable abdominal mass. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
